method: kb_search(query=item.question, limit=10, multi_query=false, use_v1=true), 1 real MCP call per holdout question, current (pre-F06) implementation. Recall/rank judged strictly against evaluation/holdout-2026-10-14.json's candidate_documents ids (no substitution, even where a topically-identical-but-differently-ided document was found -- see qualitative_notes).
methodology_caveat: Latency was measured as wall-clock delta between consecutive `date +%s%N` shell calls bracketing each kb_search call, executed sequentially by the same agent turn that reads the prior call's full result before issuing the next. This includes the agent's own per-turn dispatch overhead alongside the actual MCP/API round-trip, so these numbers are a rough proxy for 'time a caller actually waits', not an isolated server-side p50/p95 (e.g. no warm-up/cold-start separation, single-threaded, single run per question, this host's load at the time). item 'network-01' was run once before timestamp instrumentation started and has no latency value (excluded from latency stats, included in recall stats).

per_item.note: draft's note claimed a direct kb_search found this doc as top hit via a different (title-based) query; the frozen holdout's actual paraphrased question does not retrieve it in top 10 -- a real baseline gap, not a measurement error.
both candidate_documents entries (the 2026-08-02 and 2026-08-31 recurrences) appeared, at rank 6 and rank 8; best rank used.

strict miss against the registered candidate id, BUT rank-2 was tech_repo/1932298856 ("Storage Encryption - 스토리지 자체적으로 지원하는 암호화"), a document about exactly this NetApp encryption-key-sync failure mode -- arguably a better ground-truth candidate than the one frozen. Flagged for the user's consideration; did not override the frozen file mid-measurement.

strict miss against the registered incident_reports id, BUT rank-2 was support_history/CITECTS-2594, the FRB support ticket for this exact same incident (different source_type/doc id for the same real-world event) -- a cross-source-type near-miss worth noting for F05's identity/namespace discussion, not just F06 ranking.

aggregate.p95_method: nearest-rank over 29 samples (small n -- do not treat as a precise percentile)
aggregate.domain_sample_size_caveat: Per-domain N ranges from 1 to 11 (matching the approved proportional allocation) -- OpenStack/Kubernetes/Windows/Linux/Ceph each have only 1-2 questions, so their 0%/100% recall figures are not statistically meaningful on their own; they are raw counts, not estimates.

outliers_note: No item exceeded 3x the median latency (threshold ~32785ms). The two slowest items (storage-02 at 16618ms, openstack-02 at 15487ms) are within normal variance for this measurement method, not isolated anomalies -- no error, retry, or exception occurred on any of the 30 calls.
qualitative_findings_for_f06_scoping: Several current misses are not 'no relevant document exists' but 'the relevant document exists under a different id/source_type than the one the holdout recorded as ground truth' (storage-02, kubernetes-01). This is directly relevant to F05's unresolved namespace/identity-domain discussion as well as F06's ranking scope.

network-06 shows query-phrasing sensitivity: the drafting fork found the exact source document via a different (closer to title) query, but the frozen holdout's natural-language paraphrase does not retrieve it in the current implementation's top 10. This is a concrete, reproducible example of the 'question context' gap F06/R05 is meant to address.

This measurement used plain kb_search only (no graph traversal). It intentionally does NOT yet run the handoff's comparison-group B (kb_search + graph) -- that comparison, and any cost-budget decision, should happen only after the user reviews these baseline-A numbers, per the proposal's required ordering.
